chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Basri, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The prescribed penalty (hadd) of stoning in adultery (zina) is that four witnesses testify that they saw him insert and withdraw.

key_terms.أربعة شهود: Four witnesses — the minimum number of eyewitnesses required for the hadd of zina
key_terms.الزنى: Zina — unlawful sexual intercourse (adultery or fornication)
key_terms.حد الرجم: Hadd of stoning — the capital punishment prescribed for proven adultery in Islamic law
key_terms.يدخل ويخرج: Insert and withdraw — technical legal phrase describing the act of penetration that witnesses must observe

ai.seo_question: What is the evidentiary standard for the hadd of stoning in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) specifies the evidentiary standard required to impose the hadd of stoning for zina: four witnesses must each directly observe the act of penetration. This ruling reflects the classical Shia jurisprudential position that the hadd of stoning is exceptionally difficult to establish in practice, requiring eyewitness testimony of the act itself rather than mere circumstantial evidence. The stringent evidentiary requirement functioned as a practical barrier against wrongful prosecution, understood by the early community as a form of divine mercy.
